items.title: Oil retreats as US weighs futures market action

featured_image.name: Markets News, March 5, 2026: U.S. Indexes Tumble as Oil Hits $80 a Barrel; Dow Closes Down Almost 800 Points

items.description:
Markets around the world lurched through another volatile session on Thursday as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its seventh day, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average briefly plunging more than 1,000 points before oil prices pulled back from their highs on reports of possible US government intervention in futures markets.

The Dow shed 784 points, or 1.6%, closing at 47,954.74, according to The Wall Street Journal, after US crude surged past $80 a barrel for the first time since summer 2024. The S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.3%, reversing a Wednesday rally that had been fueled by reports Iran was open to indirect negotiations with Washington.[1][2][3]

items.title: Physicists create first computer model of 'ideal glass'

featured_image.name: Scientists open new window on the physics of glass formation

items.description: A team of physicists at the University of Oregon has created the first computer model of an "ideal glass," a long-theorized material in which molecules are packed as tightly and stably as possible while maintaining the disordered, amorphous structure that defines glass. The achievement, published in Physical Review Letters, addresses a challenge first posed nearly eight decades ago and could eventually reshape how advanced materials are designed and manufactured.[1][2]

items.title: Cambridge scientists discover 'molecular catapult' in solar materials

featured_image.name: Molecular 'catapult' fires electrons at the limits of physics

items.description: Scientists at the University of Cambridge have observed electrons crossing the boundary between solar materials in just 18 femtoseconds — less than 20 quadrillionths of a second — propelled by molecular vibrations acting as a "catapult." The discovery, published March 5 in Nature Communications, challenges decades of assumptions about how charge moves through solar energy systems and could reshape the design of more efficient light-harvesting technologies.[1][2]

items.title: UN report finds migratory species decline accelerating

featured_image.name: Migratory fish species are in drastic decline, a new UN report details

items.description:
The plight of the world's migratory species has worsened over the past two years, with 49 percent of populations protected under a United Nations treaty now declining and 24 percent facing extinction, according to an interim report released this week by the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS). The findings represent a sharp deterioration from the landmark 2024 assessment, which found 44 percent of species declining and 22 percent threatened with extinction.[1][2][3]

The report, developed by the UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC) and other contributors, will be presented at CMS COP15, set to convene in Campo Grande, Brazil, from March 23 to 29.[2][3]

items.title: Jimmy Lai won't appeal 20-year Hong Kong sentence

featured_image.name: Hong Kong's Jimmy Lai Decides Against Appealing 20-Year ...

items.description:
Jimmy Lai, the 78-year-old founder of Hong Kong's now-defunct Apple Daily newspaper, has decided not to challenge his conviction or 20-year prison sentence under Beijing's national security law, his legal team confirmed on Friday, bringing an end to one of the most closely watched cases in the city's history.

"We confirm we have clear and definitive instructions not to lodge an appeal against conviction or sentence," Lai's lawyers told The Associated Press and Reuters, without providing further explanation for the decision.[1][2]

items.title: SoftBank seeks record $40B loan to fund OpenAI bet

featured_image.name: OpenAI closes $40 billion funding round, largest private tech deal on record

items.description:
SoftBank Group is seeking a loan of up to $40 billion to help finance its latest investment in OpenAI, according to Bloomberg, in what would be the Japanese conglomerate's largest-ever borrowing denominated solely in dollars.[1][2]

The 12-month bridge loan will be underwritten by four lenders, including JPMorgan Chase, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Talks with banks are ongoing and details could change, the people said. Spokespeople for both JPMorgan and SoftBank declined to comment.[1]

items.title: US reports 90 percent drop in Iranian ballistic missile attacks

featured_image.name: Number of Iranian ballistic missiles fired plunges since start of Operation  Epic Fury

items.description: Iranian ballistic missile attacks have plummeted by 90 percent since the start of Operation Epic Fury, U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper announced Thursday during a press briefing at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa, Florida. Drone attacks have fallen by 83 percent over the same period, Cooper said, as U.S. and Israeli forces continue to degrade Tehran's offensive military capabilities in what has become the largest American buildup in the Middle East in a generation.[1][2]
